title: Best Practices & Security
intro: Learn the basic ideas of Best Practices & Security in simple English. Read the explanation and example first; the quiz asks only from the concepts taught here.

items.heading: PEP 8
items.text: PEP 8 is the main style guide for Python code. It covers conventions that improve consistency and readability.

items.heading: Meaningful names
items.text: Names such as total_price and user_name communicate intent better than unclear names.

items.heading: DRY
items.text: DRY means “Don’t Repeat Yourself”. Avoid unnecessary duplication when a reusable solution is clearer.

items.heading: KISS
items.text: KISS encourages keeping solutions simple and understandable rather than adding needless complexity.

items.heading: Input validation
items.text: Validate external input so unexpected or unsafe data does not reach sensitive operations unchecked.

items.heading: Password security
items.text: Passwords should be stored using a suitable password-hashing method, not as plain text.

items.heading: SQL injection
items.text: Parameterized SQL queries separate user data from SQL commands and help reduce SQL injection risk.

items.heading: Least privilege
items.text: Give users, programs and services only the permissions they actually need.

items.heading: Secrets
items.text: API keys, passwords and private tokens should not be hardcoded into public source code.

items.heading: Dependencies
items.text: Keeping dependencies updated helps receive bug fixes and security fixes.

items.heading: Code review
items.text: Reviewing code can catch defects, security issues and maintenance problems before they become larger issues.

items.heading: Safe errors
items.text: Error messages should help the developer or user without exposing secrets or internal sensitive details.
